title: Austin ICE shooting: Man in detention center ‘with a bullet in his back,’ lawyer says | CNN
text:
Source: CNN

An Immigration and Customs Enforcement agent shot and wounded a man from Venezuela who was working as a DoorDash driver Sunday in Texas’ capital, city officials confirmed, with protests erupting at the scene against President Donald Trump’simmigration crackdown.

More than a day later, the man – whose lawyer identified him as a Venezuelan immigrant – said he had not been treated properly for the gunshot wound or received pain medication.

Federal authorities have not said what led up to the shooting in North Austin, which is at least the third involving immigration agents in Texas since the start of Trump’s second term, with criticism of heavy-handed tactics on the rise andpollsshowing most Americans against the president’s immigration policies.

Two months ago, ICE agents fatally shot a Mexican man duringa traffic stop in Houston. Two teens – US citizens – said they were attacked earlier this month by ICE agents in Alamo, Texas, after they recorded an immigration stop, with video showing one being repeatedlypunched in the headwhile pinned to the pavement. Last month, ICE officer Christian Castro waschargedwith lying about his shooting of a Venezuelan man in Minnesota and is currently free on bond after pleading not guilty.

“This is a pattern – it’s a disturbing pattern – and it’s got to stop,” said U.S. Rep. Greg Casar, a Democrat who represents part of Austin.

The man shot Sunday was identified as Wilber Rafael Garces Perez, 28, by Kate Lincoln-Goldfinch, an immigration lawyer who said she is representing his family.

Garces Perez was shot in the torso just before 1 p.m. Sunday, officials said. He was released from the hospital later in the day and detained in an infirmary at the South Texas ICE Processing Center in Pearsall, more than 100 miles away from Austin, Lincoln-Goldfinch told CNN on Monday.

“They sent him to (an ICE facility) with a bullet in his back without pain medication, and he slept overnight in a processing center without a bed,” she said.

Speaking through a translator on the phone during a Monday afternoon news conference, Garces Perez said, “I am not doing well due to the gunshot wound, and I have not received the medical attention that I require.” He said doctors did not remove the bullet because it was close to his spine.

Garces Perez has lost movement on the “entire left side of his body,” meaning he is “facing paralysis,” Lincoln-Goldfinch later told CNN’s “Erin Burnett OutFront.”

Later Monday, Lincoln-Goldfinch said in avideo on social mediathat she was told by a fellow inmate that Garces Perez had been taken to a hospital. She told CNN she didn’t have an update on his condition.

The reported transfer came after a representative of Rep. Joaquin Castro’s office visited the Pearsall facility andsaidICE were going to take Garces Perez back to the hospital, noting he was in “tremendous pain.” Castro, a Texas Democrat who represents part of San Antonio, has been vocal about immigrants detained across the state’s detention centers.

Lincoln-Goldfinch said earlier she had to use “back channels” to determine where Garces Perez was being held. The Department of Homeland Security said Garces Perez had a final order for removal, and ICE recently removed the location of such detainees from an online database, complicating their attorneys’ efforts to prevent their deportation,The Associated Press reported Monday.

So far, the Department of Homeland Security has not given a detailed account of what happened or responded to CNN’s request for comment on the circumstances of the incident.

ICE officers were conducting targeted immigration enforcement operations Sunday based on license plate checks when they came across a vehicle registered to Garces Perez, according to a source familiar with the incident.

Officers conducted a vehicle stop and questioned Garces Perez, who had a brief exchange with the officers before he fled the scene in his car, the source said. It is unclear whether Garces Perez’s car came to a complete stop or was moving during the initial exchange. The shooting happened later.

Garces Perez said through the translator the SUV tried to hit him, which he originally interpreted as an aggressive driver. When he realized ICE agents were in the vehicle, Garces Perez said he asked to pull over to be detained but the federal official denied his request.

When he attempted a U-turn to park the car, the SUV ran into his car and he was then shot, Garces Perez said, according to the translator.

Garces Perez said after he was shot, an officer went into his car and “forcibly turned it off.” He told the officer he was in pain and felt like he was going to pass out shortly before emergency medical services arrived.

The shooting was captured on video by Heidi Clark, who was livestreaming to Facebook while driving down Research Boulevard. As she neared the intersection with Anderson Square, her monologue was interrupted by loud tire screeches.

“Woah!” Clark said as she turned her phone camera toward the scene and a person could be seen in the distance running out of an SUV toward a blue sedan. Her surprise quickly turned to shock as gunfire broke out.

“Oh my God!” said Clark. “Holy f**kin’ sh*t, dude!”

Garces Perez is later seen sitting on the ground invideo obtained by ABC News, hands cuffed behind him, his shirt cut open to reveal what appears to be a gaping gunshot wound in his back.

Garces Perez is an undocumented immigrant from Venezuela who had a final order for removal, DHSsaid in a post on X. He was stable and “in federal custody pending removal,” the agency said.

Homeland Security Investigations, DHS’ investigative branch, will lead the investigation with assistance from the FBI, the post said without providing further details.

However, Lincoln-Goldfinch said Garces Perez legally entered the country through CBP One, a Biden-era program, to seek asylum. He was allowed into the country and issued a work permit while he went through immigration proceedings. The Trump administration has since ended the program.

“He had a pending court date, and the immigration court changed his court date without notifying him,” resulting in her client receiving a removal order in absentia, Lincoln-Goldfinch said.

Garces Perez was fleeing the pursuit Sunday because all he knew was an unmarked “big black truck” had rammed his vehicle twice, she said. Austin Police Chief Lisa Davis told reporters Sunday there may have been a foot chase with the ICE agent but cautioned the information was preliminary and she had not yet been briefed by federal partners.

“There was not a foot chase as they said that there was,” Lincoln-Goldfinch told CNN. “He didn’t even know he was dealing with ICE until he was shot.”

Video of the aftermath showed a blue Toyota Corolla with damage to the front passenger door and at least two apparent bullet holes in the right rear window, according to footage shared byCNN affiliate KVUEand several witness videos taken at the scene.

The Travis County District Attorney’s office has requested an independent investigation of the shooting, saying in astatementSunday the DA’s office and the Austin Police Department should be “co-equal partners in the investigation.”

Austin’s Democratic Mayor Kirk Watson also said an investigation would take place involving the Texas Rangers and Austin police.

“While I’m unhappy and I’m angry about it, I’m not surprised at all,” Watson said. “It’s happened in other cities with the nature of ICE and the way ICE is doing its business these days.”

“I see ICE following their same PR pattern in this case,” Lincoln-Goldfinch told CNN on Monday. “There is no evidence to be seen that Wilber was doing anything but driving his car down the road.”

CNN has reached out to Republican Gov. Greg Abbott’s office for comment.

The Trump administration has surged immigration agents to several Democrat-run American cities, including Los Angeles, Chicago and Minneapolis. Federal officers have fatally shot at least four people, including two American citizens, during operations across the country.

Negative reaction to ICE actions from Latino communities has resulted in a noticeable drop in support for the enforcement policies in the demographic group that was key to President Trump’s 2024 election victory.

About seven in 10 Latinos said the administration was doing too much to deport immigrants, according to aJuly pollby the Pew Research Center, with a third of Hispanic voters who cast a ballot for Trump in 2024 now saying the administration’s policies have been harmful to Hispanics.

The political reality as midterms approach was demonstrated starkly last week when Rep. María Elvira Salazar – a Florida Republican and strong supporter of President Trump generally – released acampaign adaddressing Trump directly.

“The same Hispanics who helped you get to the White House in 2024 feel betrayed today,” she said. Salazarrepresents a districtthat favored Trump by 15 percentage points in the last presidential election.

For decades, Democrats in Texas have struggled to get Hispanic voters to turn up at the polls and for those who do, the trend over the past 10 years has beenshifting away from the party, according to a voting analysis published in 2024.

Though a majority of Hispanic voters still vote blue, 40% voted Republican in the state’s gubernatorial race in 2022, and the party won by as much as 17 points in House races considered competitive by UnidosUS, a Hispanic civil rights organization. In 2024, Trump managed to flip four counties in the Rio Grande Valley that had long voted Democrat and all have Hispanic populations of over 80%.

While Texas is a Republican-led state, its capital city, Austin, leans heavily blue.

Representatives from the League of United Latin American Citizens, the Latino civil rights organization founded in Texas; the NAACP; county commissioners; members of Congress and others held a news conference in Austin on Monday afternoon.

Speakers lined up in support of Garces Perez and called for accountability for ICE.

US Rep. Lloyd Doggett told Austin residents to continue speaking out and “carry the protest to the polls.”

He also encouraged people to protest using both the Mexican and American flags.

“I want to see this protest and our demand for action wrapped in the American flag, because what could be more un-American than a secret police force that is out preying on residents of our communities?” Doggett said. “We need to reject that, and we need to reject the un-Americanism that is reflected in these terrible policies.”

On-duty ICE and Customs and Border Protection agents during the second Trump administration have shot at least 20 people, eight fatally, prior to Sunday, according to a CNN analysis.

Casar told reporters the city has seen an ICE surge come to the capital, particularly in north-central Austin, where Sunday’s shooting occurred.

“ICE needs to get out of our city and start telling people the truth,” Casar said. “We need the facts in this case to really understand what fully happened, but what we are seeing from ICE in Texas and across the country is unacceptable.”

Casar noted the fatal shootings ofRenee GoodandAlex Prettiin Minneapolis, in which DHS officials originally depicted the anti-ICE protesters as “domestic terrorists” despite videos appearing to show them moving away from agents who opened fire.

DHSturned over some evidenceto state officials in July but still has not released investigative findings in those shootings.

Hours after the shooting, dozens of protesters gathered near the site of the shooting bearing anti-ICE signs and Mexican flags, shouting slogans as uninformed officers tried to contain the crowds.

“I’ve lived in Austin all my life, but from what I’ve been seeing right now, I’ve never felt more betrayed,” Jaasiel Avilva, a 22-year-old Army veteran and son of Mexican immigrants, told CNN as the raucous protest unfolded around him Sunday on the spot where Garces Perez was shot earlier that day.

“It’s just domestic terrorism,” he added.

Janney Olvera, 13, told CNN affiliate KEYE she and her mother went to the protest immediately after she finished cheerleading practice. On the side of the road, she held a Mexican flag to honor her family’s Mexican and Guatemalan heritage.

“We’re not getting any justice,” Olvera said. “This is supposed to protect our streets? I don’t think so.”

In response to Sunday’s shooting, LULAC called on Congress to establish independent oversight of immigration and to guarantee any DHS or ICE official who violates a person’s constitutional rights will be investigated and prosecuted.

“To every American, whatever your politics are, call your senators, call your congressmen, tell them that the streets of this country will not be policed without oversight, and that no one is above the law,” Roman Palomares, LULAC chair and national president, said at Monday’s news conference.

This story has been updated with additional information.

This story was written by Eduardo Cuevas in New York, Julianna Bragg in Denver and Andy Rose in Atlanta with reporting from Ed Lavandera, Ashley Killough and Boer Deng in Austin and Priscilla Alvarez in Washington.CNN’s Amanda Jackson, Sarah Dewberry, Federica Narcancio and Catherine Shoichet contributed to this report.
